title: Tesla’s ‘Full Self-Driving’ Becomes ‘Assisted Driving’ in Europe
gist: Tesla has renamed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe after Germany's transport minister called the name misleading, as it seeks an EU approval vote expected by year-end. The rebrand follows US regulatory scrutiny and a Reuters report that Tesla gave European regulators misleading safety data.

insights.claim: Tesla has renamed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe and began using the name on its European sales website.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Naming concession is the price of European regulatory access.

insights.claim: Tesla offered the name change after German Transport Minister Steffen Bilger called 'FSD' somewhat misleading; Bilger now says he will push European regulators to approve the feature as quickly as possible.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: A rename has bought political support in Germany, raising odds of EU approval.
insights.locator: Tesla offered to change the name

insights.claim: The EU will likely vote on approving the feature by the end of the year.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Year-end EU vote is the key catalyst for Tesla's European driver-assistance revenue.

insights.claim: Tesla resisted renaming for years, even defending the name in court, until California's DMV found 'Full Self-Driving' and 'Autopilot' misleading and threatened to suspend manufacturing and dealer licenses, after which Tesla dropped 'Autopilot'.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Shows regulators can force branding changes via license threats.

insights.claim: The US federal government opened a probe in March after nine incidents where FSD allegedly failed to respond to reduced visibility without warning drivers; a 2023 recall addressed non-compliance with traffic laws.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Ongoing federal investigations are a standing regulatory and recall risk.
insights.locator: But FSD has faced plenty of scrutiny

insights.claim: Reuters reported this week that Tesla presented misleading safety data to European regulators while lobbying for FSD approval, and safety researchers accuse it of misleading statistics in the US too.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Credibility questions could derail or delay approval.

insights.claim: Wider global approval of driver assistance would likely create a lucrative, software-based funding stream for Tesla, which charges $99 per month for FSD (Supervised) in the US.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Each approved market adds high-margin recurring software revenue to Tesla's story.
insights.locator: That would likely create a lucrative

insights.claim: Approvals are spreading: Australia and New Zealand last year, a provisional Netherlands permission this spring (first in Europe), and a Chinese version in May.
insights.speaker: Aarian Marshall
insights.so_what: Track the pace of market-by-market approvals as a driver of FSD revenue.
insights.locator: Australia and New Zealand approved it last year
